records.deadline_display: The MAECI programme page for ITALYOU publishes the edition, the scholarship intake and the start date, but no application deadline: "4th Edition - Academic Year 2026-2027 ... confirms the awarding of 70 new annual scholarships ... source.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI), Italy
source.as_of: ITALYOU 4th edition, academic year 2026-2027, as published on the MAECI programme page on 2026-10-05
source.raw_extract:
4th Edition - Academic Year 2026-2027

Now in its fourth edition, the program-proven highly successful in promoting Italofonia -confirms the awarding of 70 new annual scholarships worth EUR 8,000 each, disbursed over 12 monthly installments, to students from Algeria, Cameroon, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Senegal, and Tunisia . The scholarships will start on October 1, 2026.

In addition, 64 students from the 3rd edition will be eligible to renew their scholarships for the 2026-2027 academic year , provided they have met the minimum academic requirements, namely passing exams worth at least 40 university credits (CFU).
source.notes: The shard's official_source_url https://studyinitaly.esteri.it/en/italyou returned HTTP 404. MAECI's own live programme page for ITALYOU contains no application deadline at all, and it delegates the selection to the University for Foreigners of Perugia and to Italian diplomatic missions in each target country, each of which runs a national call. I did not substitute the general MAECI IRE call deadline (26 March 2026) or a single embassy's national ITALYOU call, because those are different calls for a different programme. Note for the coordinator: the 4th edition appears already concluded - the MAECI page says scholarships start 1 October 2026 and the Italian Embassy in Tripoli published the 'Graduatoria finale del bando ITALYOU' for a.a. 2026-2027 on 31 August 2026 - so a refreshed open cycle may be expected, but no official source states a future deadline.

source.raw_extract:
Application Timeline

Application Cycle / Interviews / Application Outcomes

First application cycle:  Opens on 1 January  Closes on 1 April  Mid-April to May  From mid-June

Second application cycle:  Opens on 14 July  Closes on 1 October  Mid-October to mid-November  From December

\*A\*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis
source.exact_deadline_wording: First application cycle: Opens on 1 January Closes on 1 April / Second application cycle: Opens on 14 July Closes on 1 October
source.notes: Two pages on the awarding body's own domain give different closing dates for the same AIF first application cycle: the dedicated AIF page says 'Closes on 1 April' and the A*STAR scholarship directory (https://www.a-star.edu.sg/scholarships/home/scholarships, fetched 2026-10-05) says for A\*STAR International Fellowship '**Application Deadline:** 14 April and 1 October'. The second-cycle close (1 October) agrees; the first-cycle close (1 April vs 14 April) does not. Both pages also omit a year, so neither alone would support a calendar date. Per brief section 6 this is reported as CONFLICTING with a null date rather than choosing one source. Additional caution for the integrator: the A*STAR site also renders year-stamped 'Application Period' banners (e.g. 'A*STAR International Fellowship (Research) - 14 Jul 2026 to 1 Oct 2026') on its home/search surfaces, but that banner text was not retrievable in the pages I fetched, so it is not used as evidence and any such value should be re-verified directly.

records.title: PEC-PG - Brazilian Program for Exchange Students, Postgraduate Level (PEC-PG 2027)
records.deadline_display: From December 2026, each HEI/ICT will conduct its own selection of candidates for the PEC-PG program.

source.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil (Itamaraty / MRE) with CNPq
source.as_of: PEC-PG 2027 selection process page, published Aug 28, 2025 and updated Jul 07, 2026 01:28 PM; candidate-selection stage described for a.a. 2026-2027 awards paid March 2027 to March 2028
source.raw_extract:
The selection process for the PEC-PG program will consist of the following stages:

-   From June 29th to August 13th, Brazilian institutions (HEIs/ICTs) will submit proposals to CNPq.
-   In December 2026, CNPq will publish the list of HEIs/ICTs that will be eligible to receive PEC-PG students.
-   From December 2026, each HEI/ICT will conduct its own selection of candidates for the PEC-PG program.
-   Between March 2027 and March 2028, HEIs/ICTs must begin paying out scholarships.
source.exact_deadline_wording: From December 2026, each HEI/ICT will conduct its own selection of candidates for the PEC-PG program.
source.notes: The candidate-facing stage of PEC-PG is institution-run. The only timing the official page gives for it is a month, 'December 2026', with no day, and the page explicitly instructs applicants to 'Contact the HEIs/ICTs of your interest, or access their websites, to find out how to apply'. So this is MONTH with a null deadline_date; no day was invented. The page's other explicit dates - 'Deadline for challenging the Call Notice July 9, 2026' and 'Deadline for HEIs/ICTs to submit proposals to CNPq Until August 13, 2026' - are obligations on the Call Notice and on Brazilian institutions, not on scholarship applicants, and were deliberately not used as this record's deadline.
